keyVerseText: These be the names of the mighty men whom David had: The Tachmonite that sat in the seat , chief among the captains; the same was Adino the Eznite: he lift up his spear against eight hundred, whom he slew at one time. The Tachmonite: or, Joshebbassebet the Tachmonite, head of the three. whom he: Heb. slain. he lift: See 1.Ch.11.11. whom he: Heb. slain
rootMeaning: The Hebrew noun עֵצֶן (ʻêtsen) originates from an unused root meaning to be sharp or strong, which highlights its essential characteristic as something pointed or forceful. This root sense emphasizes the physical qualities of sharpness and strength, which go beyond the common English gloss of 'spear' to suggest an instrument designed for piercing or exerting power. Thus, the literal meaning conveys not just a weapon, but the concept of effective strength and precision in battle.
usageInScripture: The word עֵצֶן appears only once in Scripture, specifically in 2 Samuel 23:8, where it is part of the name 'Adino the Eznite.' This singular occurrence limits the range of translation to essentially one, 'the Eznite,' which likely refers to a person identified by a characteristic or origin associated with this word. The consistent translation as a proper name derived from this noun suggests a strong connection between the word's meaning and the identity or reputation of this warrior, emphasizing his prowess with a spear.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding עֵצֶן as rooted in sharpness and strength enriches our appreciation of biblical descriptions of God’s warriors and the spiritual battles faced by believers. The spear, as a symbol of power and precision, reflects how God equips His people not only with physical weapons but with spiritual authority and discernment. This word reminds us that strength in the faith is both sharp and purposeful, directed by God’s hand. It points to the reality that God’s might is manifested through His chosen servants, who act decisively against opposition, embodying divine strength in their mission.
keyVerseReflection: In 2 Samuel 23:8, the phrase 'he lift up his spear against eight hundred, whom he slew at one time' highlights Adino the Eznite’s extraordinary martial skill and valor. The use of עֵצֶן here, as part of his epithet, underscores his identity as a warrior defined by the spear, a weapon symbolizing sharpness and strength. This detail enriches the narrative by illustrating not only the man’s physical prowess but also the divine empowerment behind his victory, reminding readers of the powerful instruments God employs to accomplish His purposes.
